_metadata.description: CMR Web of Belief — Partial Node/Edge Inventory (Skeleton)
_metadata.scope: T1 frameworks, T1.5 domain theories, working models, axioms, and reduction edges. T2 templates to be populated from panel outputs.

nodes.name: Predictive Processing
nodes.description: The brain generates predictions about sensory input and updates models based on prediction errors. Friston 2010, Clark 2013.

nodes.name: Salience Network Theory
nodes.description: Anterior insula and dACC form a salience network that detects behaviourally relevant stimuli and coordinates large-scale network switching. Menon & Uddin 2010.

nodes.name: Default Mode Network / Place Cells
nodes.description: Hippocampal place cells, grid cells, and the DMN encode spatial context, support episodic memory, and mediate internally-directed cognition. O'Keefe & Nadel 1978, Raichle 2015.

nodes.name: Dual-Task / Cognitive Load
nodes.description: Working memory and attention have limited capacity; environmental demands that consume these resources degrade cognitive performance. Sweller 1988, Kahneman 1973.

nodes.name: Neuromodulation
nodes.description: DA, NE, ACh, and 5-HT systems modulate cortical processing modes. Dayan computational taxonomy: DA = reward PE, NE = unexpected uncertainty, ACh = expected uncertainty, 5-HT = aversive prediction. Yu & Dayan 2005, Schultz 1998.

nodes.name: Interoception / Body Budget
nodes.description: The brain monitors and regulates the body's internal state (allostasis). Interoceptive signals contribute to affect and decision-making. Barrett 2017, Craig 2002.

nodes.name: Multisensory Integration
nodes.description: The brain integrates information across sensory modalities using statistical inference. Crossmodal correspondences, temporal binding, spatial co-registration. Ernst & Banks 2002.

nodes.name: Embodied Cognition
nodes.description: Cognition is shaped by the body's interactions with the environment. Motor-sensory coupling, enactive perception, extended mind. Clark 1997, Varela et al. 1991.

nodes.name: Circadian Biology
nodes.description: Light entrains the suprachiasmatic nucleus to regulate circadian rhythms affecting alertness, mood, sleep, and metabolism. Czeisler 1999, Cajochen et al. 2005.

nodes.name: Motor-Sensory Integration
nodes.description: Active movement generates sensory predictions; locomotion and postural control interact with spatial cognition and creativity. Oppezzo & Schwartz 2014 (walking-creativity).

nodes.name: Biophilia
nodes.description: Innate affinity for natural elements and living systems. Wilson 1984. Reduces to PP (natural scenes match evolutionary generative model) and Salience (natural stimuli engage restoration circuits).

nodes.name: Prospect-Refuge Theory
nodes.description: Preference for spaces offering both overview (prospect) and enclosure (refuge). Appleton 1975. Reduces to PP (spatial prediction of threat) and DMN/Place Cells (hippocampal encoding of refuge locations).

nodes.name: Attention Restoration Theory
nodes.description: Natural environments restore directed attention by engaging involuntary fascination. Kaplan 1995. DEMOTED from T1 during pre-pipeline assessment — subsumable under cognitive load theory.
nodes.notes: Demoted from T1. Reduction to DT (attention as limited resource) and SAL (fascination as salience-network engagement).

nodes.name: Stress Reduction Theory
nodes.description: Natural environments reduce physiological stress. Ulrich 1983. DEMOTED from T1 during pre-pipeline assessment — subsumable under interoceptive regulation.
nodes.notes: Demoted from T1. Reduction to INT (autonomic regulation) and SAL (threat detection modulation).

nodes.name: Fractal Fluency
nodes.description: Mid-range fractal dimension (D ≈ 1.3–1.5) produces perceptual fluency and aesthetic preference. Taylor et al. 2011. Reduces to PP (fractal statistics match the visual system's generative model for natural scenes).

nodes.name: Awe / Kama Muta
nodes.description: Vast or powerful stimuli that exceed current schemas trigger awe, involving need for accommodation, small-self experience, and DMN disruption. Keltner & Haidt 2003.
nodes.notes: Multi-parent reduction: PP (schema violation), NM (NE arousal), DMN (self-referential suppression).

nodes.name: Space Syntax
nodes.description: Spatial configuration (integration, connectivity, visibility) predicts movement, wayfinding, and social interaction. Hillier & Hanson 1984. Reduces to DMN (spatial cognition) and DT (wayfinding cognitive load).

nodes.name: Soundscape Ecology
nodes.description: Acoustic environment composition (geophony, biophony, anthrophony) affects restoration and cognitive performance. Schafer 1977, Pijanowski et al. 2011. Reduces to MSI (auditory-visual integration) and SAL (noise as salience signal).

nodes.name: Place Attachment
nodes.description: Repeated positive experiences in a place create affective bonds mediated by mesolimbic DA. Lewicka 2011. Reduces to NM (incentive sensitisation) and DMN (episodic memory of place).

nodes.name: Aesthetic Anchoring (Candidate)
nodes.description: First aesthetic impression of a building creates an anchoring reference that modulates subsequent evaluation. CANDIDATE — not yet promoted to formal T1.5 status. Deferred at CREATIVE-I Decision 3, pending CROSSCUT-I evaluation.

nodes.name: Barrett-Craig Two-Stage Interoceptive Processing
nodes.description: Stage 1: modality-specific interoceptive coding (posterior insula, Craig). Stage 2: constructionist affective interpretation (anterior insula, Barrett). Adopted CREATIVE-I, confirmed NEUROMOD-I.
nodes.revision_clause: Revise if neuroimaging evidence shows anterior insula performing modality-specific coding, or if posterior insula shows context-dependent processing.

nodes.name: Differential-Mode Model
nodes.description: Low environmental stimulation → divergent/exploratory processing (tonic NE, broad attention); moderate stimulation → convergent/exploitative processing (phasic NE, focused attention). Derived independently from CREATIVE-I (cognitive) and NEUROMOD-I (computational neuromodulation).
nodes.revision_clause: Revise if evidence shows stimulation level affects divergent/convergent processing identically rather than differentially, or if the NE tonic/phasic mapping to explore/exploit does not hold in architectural contexts.

nodes.name: AX1: Dose-Response Functions
nodes.description: Environmental effects follow dose-response curves (linear, U-shaped, inverted-U, threshold, saturation). Shape varies by domain.
nodes.modulation_range: Varies by domain; see panel-specific specifications

nodes.name: AX2: Habituation Dynamics
nodes.description: Neural responses to environmental stimuli habituate over time. Rate varies by mechanism (fast for sensory novelty, slow for biophilic restoration).

nodes.name: AX3: Individual Differences
nodes.description: Three-tier model: stable traits (Big Five, sensory sensitivity), developmental (age, neurodiversity), state (current mood, fatigue, task demands).

nodes.name: AX4: Perceived Control
nodes.description: Occupant perception of control over environmental conditions moderates virtually all environmental effects. Elevated to Tier A cross-cutting moderator at CREATIVE-I Decision 2. 17+ instances across panels.

nodes.name: AX5: Cultural Modulation
nodes.description: Cultural background moderates environmental preferences and responses. Effects on spatial density tolerance, nature preference specifics, thermal comfort expectations.

nodes.name: AX6: Acute vs. Chronic Effects
nodes.description: Environmental effects differ in temporal profile: some are acute (minutes), some chronic (months/years). Allostatic load accumulates over chronic exposure.

nodes.name: AX7: VR Limitation Discount
nodes.description: Evidence from VR studies carries a discount relative to field studies, due to missing multisensory richness, temporal extent, and embodied navigation. Discount is era-dependent (improving over time).

nodes.name: AX8: Coburn R² Ceiling
nodes.description: No single visual parameter explains more than ΔR² ≈ 0.04 of variance in aesthetic/affective response to built environments. Coburn et al. meta-analytic ceiling.
nodes.modulation_range: Hard ceiling: ΔR² ≤ 0.04 per individual visual parameter

edges.notes: Constrains all interoception-dependent templates to use two-stage processing
Constrains NE-dependent templates to use explore/exploit framing
Both demoted to T1.5; ART handles cognitive restoration, SRT handles physiological stress reduction. Domain partition.
Overlapping claims about why natural materials are preferred. Unresolved pending CROSSCUT-I.
VR studies of awe particularly affected by missing embodied scale cues
VR wayfinding studies lack proprioceptive navigation cues
